title: The City Where I Live
shared_passage:
Listen to Tom talking about living in Brighton. For questions 1 to 6, choose the correct answer.

Let me see. I've worked here for four years now, but for one year, I commuted into Brighton by train. But after that, I got a room in a shared house in Brighton, and I lived there for a year before I got my own flat here two years ago. Lots of people like Brighton because it's on the coast, but I grew up by the sea so that's nothing special for me. There's always plenty going on though. Festivals, shows, sports events. I like that. My friends say the nightlife is good too, but I don't go out to bars much, so I wouldn't know. My things are always getting stolen! Two bikes, a bag, two phones. And recently I read about someone who was attacked just after getting off the bus stop outside my flat! It's a shame, because most people are really friendly and care about the city. It used to be a really dirty place, but volunteers do a great job cleaning it up. Well, I used to cycle everywhere, but since my last bike was taken 18 months ago, I've used a skateboard instead. I can carry it into shops with me, or into the office. If I need to, I can take it on the bus. I don't drive. None of my friends do, because it's so hard to find places to park a car. Well, there are lots of great restaurants in the city, but I think my favourite place to eat out is a little café. It is on the edge of town, three or four miles from the city centre. It's on the beach, on the other side of the harbour. I go there in the mornings before work for a coffee and a bacon roll. It's a great start to the day before I go to the office.
